messages:
maya: Heads up — prod inference svc (svc-infer-embed) is showing extremely uneven handoff. One pod gets ~90% of connections, others idle. 5xx spike and client retries. Anyone seeing this in metrics? :eyes:
liam: yep, grabbed quick ipvs stats. ipvsadm shows one destination with 1.2M packets, others <10k. no obvious pod cpu/mem hot spots. paste: ```IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096) Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags -> RemoteAddress:Port Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn  -> 10.0.7.23:8080 rr -> 10.2.3.11:8080 Masq 1 1204320 0 -> 10.2.3.12:8080 Masq 1 9420 0 -> 10.2.3.13:8080 Masq 1 8100 0```
sarah: are we still on ipvs mode for kube-proxy? we rolled that cluster last week to ipvs. iptables behaves differently for hash distribution.
liam: kube-proxy DaemonSet has --proxy-mode=ipvs on those nodes.
nate: also seeing NIC-level retransmits on the hot node group. ethtool -S shows rx_errors and tx_aborted on mlx5 (GPU pool). could be MTU or RDMA interaction.
maya: interesting — the skewed destination is always on hosts with RDMA-enabled NICs and jumbo MTU=9000. other nodes are 1500 MTU. Could fragmentation / path mtu cause some packets to be dropped and result in ipvs preferring one backend?
sarah: ipvs uses a hash of 5-tuple; if packet loss / RSTs happen during service syns, connections might stick to a single backend that successfully completes. also conntrack state skew can make it look like traffic is concentrated.
liam: posted recent logs from kube-proxy on the hot node: ```E0301 09:12:01.123 kube-proxy.go:xxx] Failed to sync proxier: error listing endpoints: EOF``` not super helpful. Also saw many `Invalid argument` from ipvs when trying to add destination.
nate: quick checks I ran: `ip link show` shows inconsistent MTU (9000 vs 1500). `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward` okay. ethtool counters: ```rx_errors: 1245 rx_missed: 0 tx_aborted: 98``` RDMA counters via `ibdev` show a few link recovery events.
maya: Ops question — do we have any service-level sessionAffinity turned on? That would exacerbate stickiness.
sarah: svc-infer-embed spec: `sessionAffinity: None`, endpointSlices in place.
liam: rolling a small repro: hitting svc w/ 100 concurrent short requests across 20 pods. reproduces locally only if some nodes have MTU mismatch. if I change MTU on test nodes to match 1500, distribution evens out.
maya: for immediate mitigation I propose: 1) cordon+drain the RDMA-enabled nodes from the public nodepool for this service (nate is doing), 2) restart kube-proxy on those hosts, 3) temporarily set `maxSynBacklog`/conntrack tuning?
nate: cordoned node-gpu-12 and drained. restarting kube-proxy on affected nodes now. will monitor. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Canary rollback triggered for svc-infer-embed -> rollback to last working revision by ops (auto).
liam: after drain + kube-proxy restart, 5xxs dropped ~40% within 2 minutes. traffic distribution looks much better. still want a long-term fix.
sarah: long-term items: audit MTU across cluster (should standardize), check RDMA NIC firmware/drivers, evaluate conntrack and ipvs kernel version (there are known ipvs hashing fixes in newer kernels), consider enforcing node labels + topologyKeys so service endpoints avoid mixing MTU/RDMA classes, or create a service-per-node-pool split for GPU vs non-GPU workloads.
maya: agree. I'll open infra-ticket with checklist: MTU inventory, NIC firmware matrix, kernel/ipvs versions, reproduce steps and a small perf test. assign to eng-infra + eng-runtime. Thanks for the quick run.
liam: also adding a one-off alert to warn when ipvs packet distribution >70% skew across destinations for a svc. that would've caught this earlier.
ate: note: please don't change jumbo MTU on prod GPUs without a maintenance window — firmware and SR-IOV implications. we'll do audit then plan coordinated change.
maya: closing thread for now. follow-up ticket: INFRA-2543. :white_check_mark:
